Multi-cancer early detection screening will lead to better health outcomes and cost savings.

TRICARE’s coverage of these tests is a major win for service members and their families.

I’m proud to co-sponsor legislation to provide this same coverage to Medicare recipients.

Chemical abortions destroy human life and often come with serious or life-threatening side effects for women.
 
The FDA needs to reevaluate the medical and societal risks involved with allowing mifepristone on the market.
https://t.co/GX4KTTXhSK

For far too long, America has faced a drug shortage that not only threatens patients’ health but poses a national security risk.

I am proud to join @SenGaryPeters in reintroducing the RAPID Reserve Act to end U.S. overreliance on China for access to essential medications. 
https://t.co/ZnTH0a098M

I was proud to oppose the Kaine War Powers Resolution on Iran, a ridiculous political exercise given the limited & targeted nature of last weekend's strikes. 

It could prohibit the U.S. from defending our ally, Israel, & @POTUS was well within his Article II authority to act.

3/x Through a budgeting gimmick, states have required medical providers to pay the state's fair share of Medicaid costs.
 
Why would they agree to do this?
 
Because providers get this money back—often in spades. States leverage this to receive as much as 9 to 1 federal dollars.

4/x For patients who Medicaid was intended to serve—single mothers, disabled folks, and children—the federal government is required to cover a significantly lower portion of the cost compared to patients added to the program under Medicaid expansion.

6/x States inflate their payments to providers & divert some of the federal funds to backfill their own state budgets for their political pet projects.
 
That money is supposed to be for "Health," but it can be a slush fund.
 
That means higher premiums & costs for you.

7/x If we continue the current trend, federal Medicaid subsidies could reach $5.4 TRILLION over the next ten years.
 
These costs would leave the federal government unable to care for the most vulnerable. https://t.co/PxrY1h2bIk

8/x So, what are we doing about this in the One Big Beautiful bill?
 
We're implementing responsible reforms to Medicaid to make sure that when Americans fall on hard times, they can access Medicaid funds as intended.

9/x We're curbing the provider tax gimmick, so states can't take advantage of federal taxpayers.
 
We're giving able-bodied adults on Medicaid a choice to work or volunteer if they wish to continue receiving Medicaid benefits.

We're removing illegal immigrants from Medicaid.

10/x Nobody is voting to take away Medicaid benefits from patients for whom Medicaid was designed to serve.
 
Senate Republicans are trying to slow the rate of exponential cost increases for a program we all agree must survive for future generations.

Great to meet with @DukeEnergy's Journeyman lineworker Matt Martinka and line apprentice Nathan Curlee today to honor them for their efforts in restoring energy to the Asheville VA Medical Center after Hurricane Helene. 

Read more about their story here: https://t.co/wq80gImLy2 https://t.co/st0Dvhr3Ku

Met with ag leaders in Gates Co. to discuss how the One Big Beautiful Bill delivers for family farms—enhanced crop insurance, disaster aid, crop protections, & an increased death tax exemption.

I’ll keep fighting for ag policies that keep farming strong for future generations. #100CountyTour

Later today, the Senate will vote on several government funding bills.

Instead of a clean, bipartisan bill, Leader Schumer is demanding $1.5T in additional spending—while gutting investment in rural healthcare.

Families in rural NC shouldn’t pay the price for partisan games.
